64340-woman-in-political-evolution.title: Evolution
64340-woman-in-political-evolution.creator: JOSEPH McCABE
64340-woman-in-political-evolution.description: A book by JOSEPH McCABE. Nations that had slept undisturbed through the political storms that shook Europe during three generations are now waking to revolt; classes that had witnessed the upheavals of the nineteenth century with dull indifference or shrinking apprehension now take up the world-cry of change with the energy of pioneers. The routine of daily life is distracted with the flash of a dozen new ideals.

64710-hostage-of-tomorrow.title: Hostage Of Tomorrow
64710-hostage-of-tomorrow.creator: Unknown
64710-hostage-of-tomorrow.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "Unless the jerk they picked up back in Freiburg sold Intelligence a fairy story, the Herr Doktor had some kind of a hideout here, where he was doing experiments--something that impressed the Nazis enough they were willing to finance him and leave him alone."

arxiv-2103-14335.title: The future influence of six exoplanets on the envelope properties of their parent stars on the giant branches
arxiv-2103-14335.creator: Ivan Rapoport, Ealeal Bear, Noam Soker
arxiv-2103-14335.description: Abstract We study the evolution of six exoplanetary systems with the stellar evolutionary code mesa and conclude that they will likely spin-up the envelope of their parent stars on the red giant branch (RGB) or later on the asymptotic giant branch (AGB) to the degree that the mass loss process might become non-spherical.

arxiv-2109-14953.title: About One-point Statistics of the Ratio of Two Fourier-transformed Cosmic Fields and an Application
arxiv-2109-14953.creator: Ming Li, Jun Pan, Pengjie Zhang, Jie Wang, Longlong Feng, Liang Gao, Xi Kang, Guoliang Li, Weipeng Lin, Haihui Wang
arxiv-2109-14953.description: Abstract The Fourier transformation is an effective and efficient operation of Gaussianization at the one-point level. Using a set of N-body simulation data, we verified that the one-point distribution functions of the dark matter momentum divergence and density fields closely follow complex Gaussian distributions. The one-point distribution function of the quotient of two complex Gaussian variables is introduced and studied.

arxiv-2111-15027.title: Charging up Boosted Black Holes
arxiv-2111-15027.creator: Prakruth Adari, Roman Berens, Janna Levin
arxiv-2111-15027.description: Abstract Contrary to a prevailing assumption that black holes would swiftly discharge, we argue that black holes can charge preferentially when boosted through an ambient magnetic field. Though the details are very different, the preference for charge is related to the precipitation of the Wald charge on a spinning black hole in an ambient magnetic field.

arxiv-2203-05583.title: LINNA: Likelihood Inference Neural Network Accelerator
arxiv-2203-05583.creator: Andrés N. Salcedo
arxiv-2203-05583.description: Abstract Bayesian posterior inference of modern multi-probe cosmological analyses incurs massive computational costs. For instance, depending on the combinations of probes, a single posterior inference for the Dark Energy Survey (DES) data had a wall-clock time that ranged from 1 to 21 days using a state-of-the-art computing cluster with 100 cores.

arxiv-2311-09514.title: Know Thy Neighbors: A Graph Based Approach for Effective Sensor-Based Human Activity Recognition in Smart Homes Journal: IMWUT Volume: 0 0 0 0 DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX CCS: Human-centered computing Ubiquitous and mobile computing CCS: Computing methodologies Machine learning CCS: Human-centered computin
arxiv-2311-09514.creator: Srivatsa P, Thomas Plötz
arxiv-2311-09514.description: Abstract . There has been a resurgence of applications focused on Human Activity Recognition (HAR) in smart homes, especially in the field of ambient intelligence and assisted living technologies. However, such applications present numerous significant challenges to any automated analysis system operating in the real world, such as variability, sparsity, and noise in sensor measurements.

arxiv-2501-17857.title: Planetesimal formation in a pressure bump induced by infall
arxiv-2501-17857.creator: Haichen Zhao (赵海辰), Tommy Chi Ho Lau (劉智昊), Tilman Birnstiel, Sebastian M. Stammler, Joanna Dra̧żkowska
arxiv-2501-17857.description: Abstract Context. Infall of interstellar material is a potential non-planetary origin of pressure bumps in protoplanetary disks. While pressure bumps arising from other mechanisms have been numerically demonstrated to promote planet formation, the impact of infall-induced pressure bumps remains unexplored. Aims.

arxiv-2510-07133.title: A Digital Twin Framework for Metamorphic Testing of Autonomous Driving Systems Using Generative Model
arxiv-2510-07133.creator: Tony Zhang ∗ , Burak Kantarci ∗ , Umair Siddique ∗∗
arxiv-2510-07133.description: Abstract Ensuring the safety of self-driving cars remains a major challenge due to the complexity and unpredictability of real-world driving environments. Traditional testing methods face significant limitations, such as the oracle problem, which makes it difficult to determine whether a system’s behavior is correct, and the inability to cover the full range of scenarios an autonomous vehicle may encounter.

arxiv-2512-18320.title: Deterministic Reconstruction of Tennis Serve Mechanics: From Aerodynamic Constraints to Internal Torques via Rigid-Body Dynamics
arxiv-2512-18320.creator: Sun-Hyun Youn
arxiv-2512-18320.description: Abstract Most conventional studies on tennis serve biomechanics rely on phenomenological observations comparing professional and amateur players or, more recently, on AI-driven statistical analyses of motion data. While effective at describing what elite players do, these approaches often fail to explain why such motions are physically necessary from a mechanistic perspective.

arxiv-2602-18944.title: Covering Maps with respect to Topologies on the Fundamental Group
arxiv-2602-18944.creator: Naghme Shahami, Behrooz Mashayekhy
arxiv-2602-18944.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Naghme Shahami, Behrooz Mashayekhy. In this paper, using the classical covering theory, we introduce a generalization of covering maps of a space X X with respect to a topology τ \tau on the fundamental group of X X . We show that the famous notions, covering, semicovering, generalized covering and fibration maps are special cases of this new notion π 1 τ \pi_{1}^{\tau} -covering map.

britannica-1911-silures.title: Silures (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-silures.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-silures.description: Article 'Silures' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 25), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. occupying approximately the counties of Monmouth, Brecon and Glamorgan. They made a fierce resistance to the Roman conquest about A.D. 48, but a legionary fortress (Isca Silurum, Cærleon) was planted in their midst and by A.D. 78 they were overcome. Their town Venta Silurum (Cærwent, 6 m. of Chepstow) became a Romanized town, not unlike Silchester, but smaller.

plos-pone-0010852.creator: Changhui Mao, Miao Wang, Biquan Luo et al.
plos-pone-0010852.description: PLOS ONE research article. Glucose-regulated protein 94 (GRP94) is one of the most abundant endoplasmic reticulum (ER) resident proteins and is the ER counterpart of the cytoplasmic heat shock protein 90 (HSP90). GRP94, a component of the GRP78 chaperone system in protein processing, has pro-survival prope

pmc-11493979.title: A causal role of the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in random exploration
pmc-11493979.creator: Armin Toghi, Mojtaba Chizari, Reza Khosrowabadi
pmc-11493979.description: Decision to explore new options with uncertain outcomes or exploit familiar options with known outcomes is a fundamental challenge that the brain faces in almost all real-life decisions. Previous studies have shown that humans use two main explorative strategies to negotiate this explore-exploit tradeoff.

pmc-11595934.title: Microscopic Analysis and Evaluation of Thermal Elevation and Wear of Drills for Implant Site Preparation: An In Vitro Study
pmc-11595934.creator: Lucia Memè, Fabrizio Bambini, Tommaso Pizzolante, Martina Principi, Francesco Sampalmieri, Stefano Mummolo, Bongju Kim
pmc-11595934.description: Drilling for implant site preparation generates heat, which can cause bone necrosis if temperatures exceed 47 °C for over a minute. Factors influencing heat include drill size, speed, pressure, irrigation, and tool wear. Frequent drill replacement is essential, as wear from repeated use and sterilization affects performance.

pmc-11725027.title: Multifocal Gastric Granular Cell Tumor: A Case Report
pmc-11725027.creator: Samira Saeian, Kamran B Lankarani, Mohammad Hossein Anbardar, Seyed Majid Ahmadi
pmc-11725027.description: Granular cell tumors (GCTs) of the gastrointestinal tract are rare neoplasms often detected incidentally as subepithelial lesions during endoscopic examination. The occurrence of GCTs in the gastric cavity is even rarer. So far, there have been only four reports of multifocal gastric GCTs. Our study presents the fifth case involving a middle-aged lady with incidental multifocal gastric GCT.

pmc-12618614.title: Droplet impact on plasma surfaces: an interplay of the four states of matter
pmc-12618614.creator: Jorge Ahumada Lazo, Yang Liu
pmc-12618614.description: Non-thermal plasmas such as dielectric barrier discharges (DBD) in the vicinity of liquids may induce water activation, interfacial deformation, and enhanced evaporation through charge, mass, and energy transport. Complexity increases when a solid surface is introduced into the system. Such multiphase interactions are central to plasma technologies in medicine, disinfection, wastewater treatment, and aerospace applications like flow control and de-icing.

pmc-12718288.title: Integrating real-time OUR monitoring with adaptive feeding for enhanced antibody production
pmc-12718288.creator: Xin-Ran Zhang, Qingyuan Ran, Botao Zhang, Yong-Mei He, Liang Zhao, Wen-Song Tan, Qian Ye
pmc-12718288.description: BackgroundFed-batch culture is a well-established and widely adopted platform for industrial antibody production using Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells. However, conventional fixed feeding strategies often fall short in meeting the dynamically changing nutrient demands of cells, leading to metabolic imbalance and suboptimal productivity.

pmc-12771937.title: Knowledge of fertile period and associated factors among adolescent girls and young women in Tanzania: a nationwide survey
pmc-12771937.creator: Elihuruma Eliufoo Stephano, Victoria Godfrey Majengo, Mtoro J Mtoro
pmc-12771937.description: BackgroundKnowledge of fertile period among adolescent girls and young women (AGYW; 15–24 years) is crucial for understanding and managing reproductive health, yet it remains under explored. Many AGYW possess limited knowledge about their reproductive systems and the menstrual cycle, which can lead to misconceptions regarding fertile period and contraceptive use.

pmc-13265404.title: Composite Ultrasound Score Integrating VExUS Grading and Right Ventricular Function for Predicting 90-Day Heart Failure Rehospitalization: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13265404.creator: Hui Tang, Lihua Teng, Xiurong Xing, Qiuli Niu, Yawei Guo, Xiaohui Zhu, Zhi Liu
pmc-13265404.description: PurposeSystemic venous congestion and right ventricular (RV) dysfunction are important determinants of adverse outcomes in heart failure (HF). This study evaluated the prognostic value of a Composite Ultrasound Score integrating Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) grading and multiparametric RV systolic function for predicting 90-day HF rehospitalization.

pmc-13324471.title: A large-scale seismic risk assessment framework using enhanced FEMA P-58 and Bayesian network inference: a case study of District 2, Tehran
pmc-13324471.creator: Reza Hajirostami, Mehdi Banazadeh
pmc-13324471.description: Seismic risk assessment is a probabilistic approach that evaluates the likelihood of earthquake occurrence, structural response, expected damage levels, economic losses, and potential casualties by incorporating the inherent uncertainties associated with seismic hazards and urban building characteristics. The primary objective of this study is to quantify and spatially characterize the distribution of damage states at the urban scale.

pmc-13556160.title: Post-exercise consumption of milk or Greek yogurt may support the anti-inflammatory environment following high-intensity exercise
pmc-13556160.creator: Emily C. Fraschetti, Nicholas Cheng, Monika Nguyen, Christopher G. R. Perry, Ali A. Abdul-Sater, Andrea R. Josse
pmc-13556160.description: IntroductionFollowing exercise, there is a transient increase in circulating inflammatory mediators (e.g., cytokines). This acute inflammatory response may be modulated by post-exercise nutrition. Dairy products contain many anti-inflammatory constituents that may favourably modulate exercise-induced inflammation. This study aimed to investigate how different post-exercise nutrition strategies [milk, Greek yogurt [GY], carbohydrate [CHO], or water [no nutrition]] modulate the exercise-induced inflammatory response.

pmc-13575682.title: Envisioning the next steps for machine learning models in integrated cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic care
pmc-13575682.creator: Wenze Kan, Mengqi Zhou, Peng Xu

pmc-13671456.title: Early extracranial dissemination with prolonged survival in IDH-wildtype glioblastoma: case study and comprehensive literature review
pmc-13671456.creator: Colin Burns, Cheng Chia Wu, Kei Suzuki, Grace Lee, Daniel Kim
pmc-13671456.description: BackgroundExtracranial metastasis of glioblastoma (GBM) is rare (0.4–2%) and associated with poor prognosis. For this report, “early extracranial dissemination” is defined as radiographically and histologically confirmed metastatic disease identified at or within one month of the index GBM diagnosis, distinguishing it from metastasis arising later in the disease course.
